## Design

### 2026-10-06 – I decided to start by doing what I thought was going to be simple: downloading the prerequisites. My hope was to finish designing the schematic, but I couldn't due to a huge obstacle. I've tried to do

**3h**

I decided to start by doing what I thought was going to be simple: downloading the prerequisites. My hope was to finish designing the schematic, but I couldn't due to a huge obstacle. I've tried to do hack club projects before, so I had KiCad installed on my RPI. However, there was a huge issue: the care package's symbols were made in KiCad version 10, whilie I had v9. All of RPI's installers are slow at updating applications, so when I tried Recommended Software, Pi-Apps and even the terminal, nothing worked.

Picture of error:
![20261006_03h45m02s_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/4f4e17db66c7a7b52e145ba98a25ed813ef0096ce64ffc3712a4a32c4e45863c.png)

Then, I came across the only installer software that had version 10 of KiCad: Flatpak. For those who don't know, Flatpak is sort of a more complicated version of .exe files. When I tried to install KiCad, It said I didn't have the GPG key, so I spent a long time trying to manually install it. However, at the end, I managed to download KiCad v10.

Picture of some terminal work:
![20261006_054122_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/8820c5c6677ff8595f061c204e772059ee84802476a8dd2344d05a974cfc8378.png)

Importing .sym file:
![20261006_055101_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/2d1cb5e7dff55d81e16f60431f7d749c62ba22b24c08068fd111fa2b3b0a78bb.png)

I decided to choose a BME280 for my DHT11 Alternative. It has Barometric pressure readings. Here is a bit of the wiring:
![20261006_185641_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/c78ac6943714de0706eb182dd14f18167d09b1759c85ade3769b9bc397d10582.webp)

I hope to finish the rest of the schematic today...

### 2026-10-09 – Over the past 2.5 days, I have finalized the hardware parts of my Starbie project, Smiley Guy. It's impossible for me to say that it was smooth-sailing after my October 6th entry. Here is a day-by-day

**9.5h**

Over the past 2.5 days, I have finalized the hardware parts of my Starbie project, Smiley Guy. It's impossible for me to say that it was smooth-sailing after my October 6th entry. Here is a day-by-day work journal containing everything I did.

OCTOBER 6th CNT.

1. I decided to give up on the BME module. It was SMD and incredibly confusing to use, so I stuck with the DHT11.

2. I decided that I wanted to make the project custom. To do this, I'll have an EC11 rotary encoder as well as a different outline than the star.

3. I finished most of my schematic with wiring the DHT11, MPU6050, ESP32 C3, as well as the buttons (all of the guide).

![20261009_064746_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/9971d9e17005618f75aae5e1cff8962e2c41af463d6178f346c20e907505cc7c.png)

TOTAL: 3hrs (Got a bit addicted ;))

OCTOBER 7th

It's time for the hard part: What's not on the guide...

1.  I decided to add a Joystick too. I really wanted my keychain to be like a game console, so this was self-explanatory...

2. To begin with, I tried finding an EC11 encoder to use. I personally like the LCSC part finder, so I use their website to find parts. I found the EC11J for a ridiculously cheap price of $2.29. This was made by Alsalpine.

EC11J:

![20261009_063522_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/bfda9ee9fd3de06e232f76a2549706f0d14de0f034f3b5ae1dd982d26a7c3586.png)

3. Now it was time for what I thought wold be possible: a joystick. It turns out the ESP32 S3 simply doesn't have enough pins, so this side quest must be cancelled.

4. Now that I have my desired part, I used SNAPEDA's database of parts and their inforrmation to find the 3d model, datasheet, as well as the footprint and the symbol for the EC11J. I imported these into KiCad.

EC11J SNAP EDA:
![20261009_063906_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/76f3615ea547fd4e3ea87559915265ba52c650bf37a312fdad2d487d536f5847.png)

5. I tried to wire this myself with the provided datasheet, but it was practically useless.

Datasheet Circuit Diagram:

![20261009_064102_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/9c3c152fc3d7b131b8c309ced45cfcde32c9b5c590c263859636403c5b46e29b.png)

6. Because of this, I decided to ask halflife on slack for help. @Meghana, the creator of this program, responded back and showed me a diagram that showed a simple circuit diagram for wiring the EC11.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/3ed5711f9195431ff642cbbf9edb13d722cb426f4f89dafc90f492c3186799f9.png)

7. I wired the encoder, with two resistors attached to ports A and B for safety.

![20261009_064754_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/5a137ef2379ec878ac1d2260ae0d2fcd4a451a8a5ca404362af8e887d083b89e.png)

8. I decided to try to make the outline for the PCB. To begin with, I tried to use the given tools inside of KiCad, which didn't end well, leading to many overlapping cuts and KiCad freaking out.

9. Then I tried to use Canva to generate a PNG, put it through remove.bg, a background remover, followed by a PNG to SVG  converter. Then, I tried importing the SVG as a graphic.

![20261008_034122_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/ac58c8828c4c63c39978884d773c85eeac8e13bf1112477a13b751372bf95cb1.png)

![20261008_034233_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/cc4177bbae2d6151489fbe2686009a7589e214a54b11f879b717da5fbc37496f.png)

![20261008_034408_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/844747cbc804a45cdb9318990053822d10a2144e9cbe4af3dcba69acd30201f9.png)

![20261008_034939_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/05efe318a52eadd52413c836b3dea38b526521cc2b97d8f9904c82aab5704e49.png)

10. As you can see, the end result in the 3D viewer was not very good. I think for some reason the poor outline was inverted.

11. I decided to sleep on this as I was too lazy to troubleshoot and didn't want to burnout.

TOTAL: 3.5 hrs

OCTOBER 8th

1. I realized that the best way to not cause the loss of data over multiple conversion and refining websites is to simply create it at the source. For around 30 minutes, I decided to bite the bullet and create a simplified outline right in KiCad. To be honest, it turned out better than Canva. (DIDN"T TAKE PICTURE, BUT HERE IS FINAL RESULT):

![20261009_070411_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/a691657461db4579389bdddd1efbfef9ae94d5217e72b0bc199ff6e6e913a024.png)

2. I started to wire the PCB, but I got way too many errors as I wired the PCB carelessly, so some wires were dangerously close to the footprints and sometimes on them. This caused around 30 errors, which I didn't know was caused by careless routing. Also, from my previous attempt at making HackPad for Blueprint, I knew how to use V to switch between PCB layers, which wasn't in the guide. This came in handy to bypass many crossovers of wires.

EG of one of many errors:

![20261009_013407_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/fc8678742600f2421547d6ff614f69f3d5cfc19001473e760f1b674fc25d5e2b.png)

3. After some help with CHATGPT, I rerouted the board efficiently.

4. After, I assigned 3d models to each footprint. This showed a huge issue in the 3d viewer. I didn't take a picture as I was genuinely mad. I realized that I put the MPU6050 Footprint as a 1x08 connector, which is significantly less wide than the actual footprint. I put the connector right next to the encoder. In the 3D view, I noticed the MPU6050 going straight through the encoder. This meant I'd have to move the encoder and reroute it. I WAS MAD. After a few minutes though, it was fixed.

5. Using the same method I attempted to use to import a graphic from Canva to the PCB Editor, I created a logo for Triple T Studios (Tung Tung Tung Sahur is the main mascot), which I put on the front and back of my PCB. I also put brainrot text on the top of the PCB, with a keychain hole in the PCB.

TOTAL: 3.5 hrs

Final Product:
